SQL Tuning

1. Using EXPLAIN
  • The EXPLAIN statement shows the query execution plan — which indexes are used, join order, scan types: 
    EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM Person WHERE city = 'NYC' AND age > 25;
  • Look for:
    • Index scans — means an index is being used (good);
    • Table scans — means a full cache scan (bad for large datasets);
    • Join type — HASH join vs NESTED LOOP join;
2. Query Parallelism
  • By default, each query runs in a single thread per node;
  • For complex analytical queries, you can increase parallelism: 
    CacheConfiguration cfg = new CacheConfiguration("analyticsCache");
cfg.setQueryParallelism(4); // use 4 threads per node
  • Higher parallelism benefits scans over large datasets but consumes more CPU;
  • Can only be set at cache creation time — not changeable later;
3. Lazy Query Execution
  • By default, Ignite fetches all results into memory before returning;
  • For queries that return large result sets, enable lazy mode to stream results: 
    SqlFieldsQuery query = new SqlFieldsQuery("SELECT * FROM LargeTable");
query.setLazy(true);
  • Lazy execution reduces memory usage but may hold locks longer;
4. Colocation-Aware Queries
  • If you know which partition holds the data, route the query directly: 
    SqlFieldsQuery query = new SqlFieldsQuery(
    "SELECT * FROM Person WHERE id = ?"
);
query.setArgs(42);

// Runs only on the node that owns partition for key=42
cache.query(query);
  • For joins, make sure tables are colocated to avoid distributed joins;
5. Memory and Resource Management
  • SQL query memory limit — limit how much memory a single query can use: 
    SqlFieldsQuery query = new SqlFieldsQuery("...");
query.setMaxMemory(50 * 1024 * 1024); // 50 MB
  • Query timeout — cancel long-running queries: 
    query.setTimeout(10_000, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
  • Page size — control how many rows are fetched per page (default 1024): 
    query.setPageSize(5000);
6. Common Performance Tips
  • Always create indexes for columns used in WHERE and JOIN clauses;
  • Use affinity colocation to make joins local;
  • Avoid SELECT * — select only the columns you need;
  • Use parameterized queries (? placeholders) instead of string concatenation for better plan caching;
  • Enable query parallelism for analytical workloads;
  • Use lazy execution for large result sets;
